blocks.text: Puolueeton snuck past in Lesson 30 as 'impartial', built from puolue + -ton. That -ton ending is actually one half of a matched pair Finnish uses to build negative or opposite adjectives — the other half is the prefix epä-. Between them, they generate a huge share of this corpus's harshest vocabulary.

blocks.title: Two ways to say 'not'
blocks.text: English mostly relies on one prefix for this job — un-, in-, dis- depending on the word. Finnish cleanly splits the job in two: epä- flips an adjective to its opposite, while -ton/-tön removes a quality from a noun entirely. Once you know both, you can decode a huge number of 'bad review' adjectives without ever looking them up.

blocks.content: {Epä-|grammar|negative prefix|un-/not} attaches to the front of an adjective (or noun) to flip its meaning. Luotettava (reliable) → {epäluotettava|grammar|epä- + adjective|unreliable}. Rehellinen (honest) → {epärehellinen|grammar|epä- + adjective|dishonest}. Ammattitaitoinen (professional, Lesson 1) → {epäammattitaitoinen|grammar|epä- + adjective|unprofessional}.

items.en: A dishonest repair shop in every respect.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — -ton/-tön: removing a quality from a noun

blocks.content: {-ton|grammar|negative suffix|-less/without} (or -tön after front vowels) attaches to the end of a noun, meaning 'without [that noun]'. Vastuu (responsibility) → {vastuuton|grammar|noun + -ton|irresponsible} — literally 'without responsibility'. Puolue (side/party) → puolueeton, 'without a side' = impartial, from Lesson 30.

items.en: They didn't take responsibility — a completely irresponsible repair shop.
An impartial repair shop revealed the truth.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — Stacking both, for maximum emphasis

blocks.title: Reviewers stack negatives for effect
blocks.text: Some of the harshest lines in the corpus stack epä- and -ton adjectives back to back: epäluotettava, eivät kanna vastuuta. This piling-up of negative adjectives is a deliberate rhetorical move — each one narrows the shop's reputation a little further, building toward a flat verdict of total distrust.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: What kind of repair shop was it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Täysin epäluotettava ja vastuuton. En suosittele kenellekään.
lines.en: Completely unreliable and irresponsible. I don't recommend it to anyone.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Whenever you meet a new adjective starting with epä- or ending in -ton/-tön, don't panic — strip the affix off, check whether you already know the word underneath (luotettava, vastuu, rehellinen), and you'll usually land on the meaning yourself, flipped or stripped exactly as this lesson describes.

blocks.content: Epäluotettava: E-pä-luo-tet-ta-va (six syllables — epä- is always light and quick, the weight sits on the word after it). Vastuuton: VAS-tuu-ton (long held 'uu' in the middle). Puolueeton: PUO-lu-ee-ton (the 'uo' glides, then a long held 'ee').

-ton/-tön — strips a quality from a noun entirely
